audit_findings.title: FY2025 OE may omit the full recurring interest burden
audit_findings.magnitude: 2026 first-half interest expense of $55.7m annualizes to $111.4m, $32.9m above FY2025; approximately $25.5m after the filed 22.4% tax rate, reducing computed values by about $6.67-$10.39 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: A full-year recurring interest charge reduces equity-level OE because interest expense is retained while debt principal is not deducted in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Interest expense increased during 2025, primarily due to higher long-term debt balances associated with the 5.25% notes due September 15, 2035 (the "2035 Notes") and the 5.55% notes due September 15, 2040 (the "2040 Notes"), which were issued on August 20, 2025, partially offset by the redemption of $400.0 million of 3.50% notes in December 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated anchor-normalization issue: FY2025 included only a partial period for the $1.0bn notes, while the 2026 filing shows the higher recurring burden. A proportional rerun would reduce bear, base and bull values to approximately $218.28, $282.94 and $330.89 per share. All remain below the $352.14 price, and the base-case buy-below threshold would decline from $204.22 to about $198.06, so the investment conclusion does not change.
audit_findings.action: Rerun all scenarios with annual interest expense of approximately $111.4m, or the subsequently filed full-year 2026 amount, and apply the normalized tax effect without deducting ordinary debt principal.

audit_findings.title: Projected growth may require acquisition spending excluded from OE
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed acquisition spending was $109.6m in FY2025 and $676.9m in FY2024; FY2025 spending equaled 13.7% of the $798.5m OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Acquisition purchase prices are reinvestment required for acquired earnings but are excluded from OE; projecting acquired growth without this cash outlay inflates OE growth and operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase in revenues in 2025 primarily reflects higher sales in our non-residential construction end-market of $30.2 million, driven by recent acquisitions, partially offset by lower sales in our residential construction end-market of $14.0 million due to decreased new construction activity.
audit_findings.explanation: The mismatch is reasonably capable of changing value materially. FY2025 revenue growth was only 0.3%, comprising negative 2.9% organic growth and positive 3.2% acquisition growth, while the valuation assumes 3%-6% growth without an acquisition-reinvestment charge. The filing does not prove that future base or bull growth requires the historical spending level, but the demonstrated spending is large relative to anchor OE and the company identifies acquisitions as a continuing strategic pillar.
audit_findings.action: Build an organic-versus-acquired revenue and OE bridge for each scenario, verify whether FY2025 OE added back acquisition costs, and rerun any scenario dependent on M&A with the required acquisition cash outlays deducted in the years incurred.

audit_findings.title: Gross cash may include customer prepayments that are not excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: June 2026 contract liabilities were $378.1m versus $665.3m of cash, or 56.8% of the cash addition; the net economic overlap is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding customer-funded cash to the equity bridge while also valuing future profits from the deferred warranty revenue can double-count the distributable portion unless future service costs and required operating cash are recognized consistently.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company receives payment at inception of contracts for separately priced extended service warranties.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed balance establishes a potentially significant customer-prepayment pool, but it does not trace those funds to the June cash balance or quantify the future service margin and cash requirements. The $378.1m liability face value is $9.28 per diluted share, but that is not an appropriate automatic deduction because Carlisle will recognize revenue and incur service costs over time. Materiality therefore remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $665.3m cash balance to the $378.1m warranty contract liability, forecast the associated revenue, service costs and claims cash flows, determine required operating cash, and rerun the bridge using only genuinely distributable excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Customer concentration creates a discontinuous downside absent from smooth growth cases
audit_findings.magnitude: The two largest customers represented 33.0% of FY2025 revenue, approximately $1,656.6m of the filed $5,019.9m total
audit_findings.mechanism: Loss of volume or customer-driven price compression would cause a step reduction in revenue, margins and OE that is not represented by the smooth growth paths.
audit_findings.evidence: In 2025 CCM's two largest customers represented 33% of the Company’s consolidated revenues.
audit_findings.explanation: The concentration is demonstrated, but no customer loss, insourcing event or abnormal pricing concession is presently reflected in the record. It is therefore a forward-looking risk rather than an identified error in current OE. Its large revenue exposure warrants explicit monitoring and stress testing, particularly because each major customer accounted for roughly 16%-17% of revenue.
audit_findings.action: Run separate stresses for loss of each major customer, partial volume migration and margin compression, using customer-level contribution margins and realistic stranded-cost assumptions; monitor distributor consolidation and purchasing behavior.

audit_findings.title: Legacy asbestos claims may be an unbridged claim on equity
audit_findings.mechanism: Net asbestos indemnity and defense cash payments attributable to discontinued businesses would reduce equity value through a bridge deduction or normalized OE charge if not already captured.
audit_findings.evidence: Since the Company’s insurance coverage contains various exclusions, limits of coverage and self-insured retentions and may be subject to insurance coverage disputes, the Company may incur expenses for indemnity and defense costs and recognize income from insurance recoveries in different periods.
audit_findings.explanation: No omitted amount is demonstrated. The FY2025 filing states that the recorded indemnity accrual was not material to financial position, results or operating cash flow, and the June 2026 filing reports no material legal developments. However, neither the gross accrual nor the insurance receivable is supplied, so the owner cannot compare the net claim with the $11,884m base equity value or determine whether timing differences are already reflected in OE.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 2026 gross asbestos accrual, related insurance receivable, defense-cost history and expected payment schedule; assess insurer collectability and bridge any net claim not already included in normalized OE.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded supplemental pensions are a small senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $17.3m supplemental/director projected benefit obligation, equal to about $0.42 per diluted share and 0.15% of the $11,884m base equity value; expected 2026 payments were $1.3m
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unfunded obligation not already reflected through pension expense is a senior claim requiring a bridge deduction or normalization of OE cash payments.
audit_findings.evidence: The executive supplemental and director defined benefit plans have no plan assets and the Company is not required to pre-fund the obligations.
audit_findings.explanation: Even deducting the entire filed $17.3m obligation from equity would reduce value by only about $0.42 per share and would not affect any scenario or the buy-below conclusion. Expected 2026 payments equal only 0.16% of the $798.5m OE anchor. The item should be reconciled to avoid double-counting, but its demonstrated scale is not material.
audit_findings.action: Confirm which pension costs and payments are already included in normalized OE, then deduct only the unreconciled obligation; no full valuation rerun is needed unless a later filing shows a materially larger liability.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2023 residual D&A was $35.6m, 17.4% of filed D&A and 4.5% of the $798.5m FY2025 OE anchor; FY2025 eligible amount and valuation effect are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Eligible non-economic D&A left as an expense understates OE and therefore understates projected operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2023 $35.6m (17.4% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: This is not a demonstrated valuation error because the residual has not been shown to qualify for an add-back or to recur at the FY2023 amount. The conservative treatment cannot overstate value. The known $35.6m scale is large enough that a recurring eligible amount could matter, including near the bull case's $10.86 per-share gap to market, but the record cannot establish that effect.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the FY2025 depreciation and amortization composition by asset and business, identify only qualifying non-economic charges, and rerun the scenarios if filed evidence establishes a recurring eligible add-back.
